top3.headline: Goldman Sachs pulls AI coding tools from most bankers and traders
top3.whyItMatters: Regulated firms are narrowing AI coding to engineers, so review who in your company runs agents.

top3.headline: Codex agents pushed OpenAI's Git below 90% reliability, so it rebuilt
top3.whyItMatters: If agents multiply your branches and pushes, source control becomes the bottleneck.

top3.headline: Anthropic's internal Claude use, at list prices, topped its monthly payroll
top3.whyItMatters: AI usage may soon rival headcount cost, so leaders need a budget line for it.

items.title: Poisoned agent memory steers decisions in later sessions, benchmark finds
items.takeaway: Agents finish the real task with no visible anomaly while serving the attacker.
items.soWhat: Treat persistent agent memory as an attack surface and audit what gets stored.

image.alt: arXiv 2611.01700: Poisoned agent memory steers decisions in later sessions, benchmark finds

items.title: 4-bit coding agents keep accuracy but change how they solve problems
items.takeaway: AWQ cut Qwen-7B one-shot solves from 17 to 0; loop-based solves rose to 25.
items.soWhat: If you run cheaper quantized agents, test their tool use and failure modes, not just scores.

image.alt: arXiv 2611.02368: 4-bit coding agents keep accuracy but change how they solve problems

items.title: Shared prompt turns a flat floor plan into a 3D house
items.takeaway: Made with Opus 5.5 and three.js; prompt and code are public.
items.soWhat: Design teams can study a public prompt for turning static plans into 3D web pages.

items.title: OpenAI raises critical bug bounties up to $172,000, plans security sprint
items.takeaway: Cathedral Systems researchers will use OpenAI models to attack OpenAI's defenses.
items.soWhat: AI-driven attacks are expected, so budget for AI-assisted red teaming of your own systems.

items.title: Builder finds adversarial AI code reviews mostly waste tokens
items.takeaway: @poteto favors empirical and formal verification and is cutting the review skill.
items.soWhat: Spend agent budget on tests and verification before adding AI reviewers.

items.title: wterm lets agents drive web terminals through WebMCP
items.takeaway: Opt-in per terminal, with a read-only mode, and no DOM scraping or fake keystrokes.
items.soWhat: Standard agent access to web apps is arriving, so plan which surfaces to expose.

items.title: LLM 0.37 ships 12 AI-assisted fixes; review was easier than expected
items.takeaway: Simon Willison triages them with Opus 5.5 or GPT-6 Astra as bug reports with examples.
items.soWhat: Maintainers can use models to triage AI-written contributions rather than reject them.

image.alt: Simon Willison: LLM 0.37 ships 12 AI-assisted fixes; review was easier than expected

items.title: Critic says GPT-6 Astra weight-reading results are not superhuman
items.takeaway: He reproduces the game-identification task with a three-line NumPy heatmap.
items.soWhat: Check claims of superhuman model abilities against simple baselines before acting on them.

image.alt: Sean Goedecke: Critic says GPT-6 Astra weight-reading results are not superhuman

items.title: Capy makes persistent orchestrating agents generally available
items.takeaway: Captains run hundreds of threads across devices; a Dock CLI runs Capy headless.
items.soWhat: Long-running agent managers are becoming products, so teams can test fleets without building orchestration.

items.title: Goldman Sachs limits Claude Code and GitHub coding tools to engineers
items.takeaway: Most bankers and traders lost access; strats are exempt, per Bloomberg.
items.soWhat: Expect tighter rules on who may run coding agents, especially in regulated firms.

items.title: OpenAI rebuilt its Git backend because Codex agents overloaded it
items.takeaway: Pando cut median push latency nearly 5x; built with Codex in 10 weeks.
items.soWhat: Agent volume breaks developer infrastructure, so stress-test source control before scaling coding agents.

image.alt: OpenAI blog: OpenAI rebuilt its Git backend because Codex agents overloaded it

items.title: Anthropic's internal Claude use outvalued its monthly payroll in April
items.takeaway: Valued at retail prices against pay excluding stock; usage up 250-fold since January.
items.soWhat: Start tracking AI usage against labor cost, because leading AI companies already do.

voices.quote: As AI becomes more capable at finding vulnerabilities, defenders need to put it to work before attackers do.
This is widespread in finance. The ban hammer is coming down.
we put them in the hands of those who are best suited to leverage them for the long term.
i have found very little value with code review in the abstract, agents tend to just get lost in the nitpicks and yagnis
Capy Captains increased my issue fixing throughput by about 5X overnight.

hotOnX.text: Adversarial AI code reviews are mostly a waste of tokens; empirical and formal verification are a better use of them
hotOnX.note: Builders spending heavily on AI reviewers want to know if the tokens pay off.

hotOnX.text: Next security sprint with Cathedral Systems, and critical bug bounty rewards up to $172,000 including bonuses
hotOnX.note: A fourfold jump in top bounties signals how seriously labs take AI-found vulnerabilities.

hotOnX.text: wterm now supports WebMCP: agents can list, read, type into and press keys in terminals on a web page
hotOnX.note: Developers want agents to use web apps through a standard, not screen scraping.

hotOnX.text: A flat floor plan builds into a 3D house in three.js, made with Opus 5.5; prompt and repo shared
hotOnX.note: Designers like seeing a full prompt and code behind a polished 3D page.
